Simulation of an assembly process from a multilayer meta-web

Source: R/metaWebNetAssemblyML.R
metaWebNetAssemblyML.Rd

Continuous time colonization-extinction model of metaWebNetAssemblyCT() in which the non-trophic layers change the extinction rates and, optionally, some species depend obligately on others (e.g. on foundation species). Losing a partner with a positive effect (a mutualist, a facilitator) raises the extinction rate of a species; losing a partner with a negative effect (a competitor) lowers it.

Usage

metaWebNetAssemblyML(
  mg,
  layers = default_layer_signs(),
  beta = c(pos = 0, neg = 0),
  m,
  e,
  se,
  time,
  layer_beta = NULL,
  obligate_on = NULL,
  type_attr = "type",
  effect_attr = "effect",
  obligate_layers = NULL,
  normalize = TRUE
)

Arguments

mg

the multilayer network: an mgraph (the list of igraph layers returned by multiweb::readMultiplex()) or any list of igraph layers, where the layer id is the list name or, if the list has no names, the type_attr edge attribute; a single igraph with the layer id in the edge attribute type_attr; or a data.frame with columns from, to, layer and, optionally, the sign column effect_attr. Vertices need a name attribute.

layers

data.frame with one row per layer: layer (the id), sign_from, sign_to and rule ("trophic" or "modifier"); see default_layer_signs(). Every layer of mg must be in it, and exactly one must have rule == "trophic".

beta

named numeric vector c(pos = , neg = ): strength of the positive and of the negative effects on the log extinction rate. With normalize = TRUE, exp(beta) is the largest factor by which the partners can change the extinction rate.

m, e, se

migration, baseline extinction and secondary extinction rates, one value or one per species, in the order of the species element of the result (the order in which species first appear in mg).

time

simulated time, the state is recorded at integer times 1 to time-1.

layer_beta

optional named numeric vector, a multiplier of beta for each layer (default 1).

obligate_on

character vector of species on which others can depend obligately (e.g. foundation species), or NULL (default) for no obligate dependence.

type_attr

name of the edge attribute with the layer id.

effect_attr

name of the edge attribute (or data.frame column) with the sign of the effect of from on to. If it is NULL or missing, the layer signs are used.

obligate_layers

layers whose positive effects create obligate dependence; NULL (default) uses all modifier layers.

normalize

if TRUE (default) the positive and negative effects on each species are divided by its number of positive and negative partners, so that the effect depends on the fraction of partners present. With FALSE the effects add up per partner present, and a species with many mutualists can become practically immortal.

Value

the list of metaWebNetAssemblyMLCT() (S, L, STime, A, rejected) with species names in STime and A, plus metaW, M, Dep and species from build_multilayer_assembly().

Details

The extinction rate of species \(i\) while species are present is $$e_i(t) = e_i \exp(\beta_- f^-_i(t) - \beta_+ f^+_i(t))$$ where \(f^+_i(t)\) and \(f^-_i(t)\) are the fractions of the partners of \(i\) with a positive and a negative effect on it that are present at time \(t\) (normalize = TRUE, the default). Thus \(\exp(\beta_+)\) and \(\exp(\beta_-)\) are the largest factors by which the partners can lower or raise the extinction rate. Migration and the trophic rule (a predator without prey goes extinct with rate se) are as in metaWebNetAssemblyCT(). With obligate_on, a dependent species goes extinct with rate se when none of the species it depends on is present.

The parameters beta (and layer_beta) are translated by build_multilayer_assembly() into the matrix M of effects on the log extinction rate used by the C++ core metaWebNetAssemblyMLCT(). Call build_multilayer_assembly() to check how a network was translated.

With beta = c(pos = 0, neg = 0) and obligate_on = NULL the model is metaWebNetAssemblyCT() on the trophic layer.

See also

build_multilayer_assembly(), default_layer_signs(), vignette("multilayer-assembly")

Examples

ed <- data.frame(from  = c("alga", "grazer", "alga",       "grazer2", "grazer"),
                 to    = c("grazer", "fish",  "grazer2",   "fish",    "grazer2"),
                 layer = c("Trophic", "Trophic", "Trophic", "Trophic", "Competition"))
r <- metaWebNetAssemblyML(ed, beta = c(pos = 1, neg = 1), m = 0.1, e = 0.05, se = 0.5, time = 100)
r$STime[, 99]
#>    alga  grazer grazer2    fish 
#>       1       1       0       0
